Hello :wave:
Does Roc have built in templating that can be used for creating HTML for HTTP servers?
Or is there a good library for this?

Rocky said:

That, is something I cannot answer better than a LLM.
Also I feel you should move this to a new topic. You might got confused by Zulip layout. You are replying to a existed topic under 'Beginners' rather than posting a new one.
3 messages were moved here from #beginners > Extra copies in generated code for a equivalent rewrite by Anton.

Hi @Rocky,
There is rocstache, I think it is inseparable from roux though.
There is also https://github.com/isaacvando/rtl but that one is not up to date with current Roc.
roc-html uses a slightly different approach but it may still suit your needs, it also needs to be updated though.

If you are looking to make your own server platform, Anton is right, Rocstache templating is tied to the roux platform.

But, if you are looking to make a webapp, consider trying roux. It includes typed db queries+migrations, and fully typed Roc-flavored templates, as well as SSE support. It is tuned for dynamic HTML as well as hypermedia style AJAX e.g. htmx or datastar.

Its super fast: (benchmark) and we have an on boarding tutorial here: https://github.com/Eldhus/roux-tutor
